moat_against: Commodity product — no switching costs; buyers shop on price and incentives
No through-cycle pricing power — incentives 9.9% of gross sales Q4 2025; gross margin 27.0% → 25.0% YoY
Land bought in competitive open market; land-heavy model traps cash in inventory (vs NVR's land-light model)
Demand hostage to mortgage rates and affordability — macro, not company, controlled
Deeply cyclical — OE/share range >3x over the last 5 fiscal years
moat_for: #3 US homebuilder scale — national purchasing leverage, 47 markets, ~235k controlled lots
Del Webb active-adult brand leadership — highest gross margins, demographic tailwind
Diversified buyer mix (2025 closings: 38% first-time / 40% move-up / 22% active adult)
Fortress balance sheet — net cash, 12.3% debt-to-capital, return-focused model with disciplined spec inventory
Pulte Mortgage capture rate 85% — financial-services margin on top of homebuilding
moat_justification: Third-largest US homebuilder with real scale advantages (national purchasing, 47 markets, ~235,000 controlled lots) and the Del Webb active-adult franchise, the segment's margin leader riding a demographic tailwind. But the product is a commodity: no switching costs, no through-cycle pricing power (incentives hit 9.9% of gross sales in Q4 2025; gross margin fell from 27.0% to 25.0% in a year), land is bought in a competitive open market and the land-heavy model consumes the cash the earnings imply, and demand is hostage to mortgage rates and affordability. OE/share has spanned >3x in 5 years. That is a weak-to-moderate moat: 4/10, CAP 7.2 years.
name: PulteGroup, Inc.
one_liner: Quality cyclical homebuilder, moat 4/10 — TTM owner's earnings do not clear 15% at $113.08 (weighted IRR 9.7%, weighted IV@15% $64.35); the price only clears the hurdle below ~$64.
